findings.message: Anchor the placeholder alternative at the start of the input. The missing ^ allows malformed provider IDs with leading text to pass validation, violating the required aws:/// prefix.
findings.evidence: The new second alternative begins with aws rather than ^aws, and FindStringSubmatch can match a suffix. For example, xaws:///zone/i-placeholder-a is accepted; the subsequent id[7:] split produces Name="zone". Both alternatives in the original regex were start-anchored.

findings.message: Preserve the complete placeholder name after the zone separator. Selecting splitted[1] discards subsequent slashes and name components, violating the placeholder-name contract.
findings.evidence: For aws:///zone/i-placeholder-a/segment, validation succeeds, but strings.Split followed by splitted[1] returns Name="i-placeholder-a". The original placeholder capture returned "i-placeholder-a/segment". The resulting reference is passed to manager/cache methods at lines 140, 176, and 336; their downstream behavior is unavailable.

result.coverage: Inspected TASK.json, CHANGE.diff, the complete staged source, and all local AwsRefFromProviderId callers. Compared both regex alternatives and name extraction with the original implementation. ProviderID remains preserved. Ordinary names with an optional suffix retain their previous extraction behavior and are not reported.
limitations: Manager/cache implementations and the placeholder prefix definition are not supplied; placeholder examples use the explicit task contract. Downstream lookup or deletion outcomes cannot be established.
result.contribution: Established two distinct contract violations through concrete input traces and source comparison; excluded unchanged ordinary-name suffix handling and limited downstream claims to visible reference propagation.
